messages:
sam: FYI ap-southeast1 is showing a spike in NVMe write latency and GPU attach retries since 03:12 UTC. IOPS graphs look normal but write latency tail is weird.

leah: saw that. appears when nightly backfill and janitor scrubs overlap. both run at high priority. suspects: write amplification from overlapping metadata writes.

peter: quick snapshot from one host: ```iostat -x 1 3
avg-cpu:  %user   %nice %system %iowait  %steal   %idle
           10.2    0.0    6.5    14.1     0.0   69.2
Device            r/s     w/s   rkB/s   wkB/s rrqm/s wrqm/s  aqsz  await r_await w_await  svctm  %util
nvme0n1         12.00   420.00  1024.0  81920.0  0.00   10.00   32.0  42.1   1.0    45.4    1.8   78.5
```

peter: note high wkB/s with modest r/s -> write-heavy, queuing at device.

storage-bot: Detected: 18 nodes with >150ms 99th write latency, 27 drives with elevated program/erase cycles. Affected pool: ap-southeast1-ephemeral-b.

leah: mitigation proposal: 1) lower janitor and backfill IO priority by moving them to background cgroup (cpu.weight/io.max) 2) enable janitor "staggered windows" so scrubs don't coincide with backfills 3) place a soft hold on new large GPU batch launches to ap-southeast1 for 2 hours.

ops-qa: routing rule ready. I'll block scheduling of jobs with gpus>4 into ap-southeast1 for 120m. small jobs still OK.

sam: running a hot patch to janitor config: ```janitor:
  io_priority: background
  stagger_windows: true
  max_parallel_scrubs: 1
  scrub_rate_limit_mb_s: 15
backfill:
  io_priority: background
  max_workers: 4
```

janitor-bot: applied config patch by sam. New scrub_rate_limit_mb_s=15, max_parallel_scrubs=1.

peter: started warm probe on 4 nodes after patch. preliminary attach attempts down to 14 failures in last 10m (was ~120). latency 99th reduced from 310ms -> 92ms on tested hosts.

vendor-support: we correlate with a firmware cohort where FW 5.2.0 has known GC behaviour causing higher tail when concurrent CTRL writes. Recommending a firmware update to 5.3.1 which changes GC windows. Need maintenance window for full rollout.

leah: firmware rollout planning: prefer to sequence by host pack, do 5% canary, monitor attach metrics for 15m, then ramp. Avoid running janitor/backfill during pack updates.

sam: cost note: if this prolongs, we should plan a temporary dedicated capacity transfer of ~40 GPUs to ap-southeast1 to keep customer SLAs while drives heal. ops-qa, what's the estimated spend?

ops-qa: rough calc ~$1.6k/hr for 40 GPUs on reserved burst. We can source from spare dedicated pool for up to 6 hours before billing impact is notable.

peter: next actions: 1) monitor the region for 30m, 2) keep routing rule for large jobs, 3) schedule firmware canary in 45m with vendor-support, 4) keep janitor/backfill throttled and staggered.

sam: thanks. I'll update the incident doc and ping product if SLAs may be impacted. Reopen thread if attach rates climb. :white_check_mark:
